title: Indian Tourist Killed, Three Injured as Two Helicopters Collide Near Everest
excerpt: A Fishtail Air and an Air Dynasty helicopter collided while landing at Pheriche at 8:11 a.m. on Tuesday. Police named the dead man as 47-year-old Vasanth Kumar Balaramaramadu; an Indian-origin New Zealand resident and both pilots were injured.
body:
• Two helicopters collided while landing at Pheriche, on the way to Everest Base Camp, at about 8:11 a.m. local time on Tuesday, Nepal Police said.
  • Vasanth Kumar Balaramaramadu, a 47-year-old Indian national aboard the Fishtail Air helicopter, was killed, police said.
  • Shailesh Krishna Patel, a 49-year-old Indian-origin resident of New Zealand, was injured and airlifted to Mediciti Hospital in Kathmandu; both pilots were also injured and taken to Kathmandu for treatment.
  • The Dynasty Air helicopter was carrying only cargo, and Fishtail Air said its aircraft was carrying passengers rescued from the Everest region when it crashed while landing.

An Indian tourist was killed and three other people were injured when two helicopters collided while landing at Pheriche, in Nepal's Solukhumbu district on the route to Mount Everest Base Camp, on Tuesday morning. The helicopters, operated by Fishtail Air and Air Dynasty, collided at around 8:11 a.m. local time, according to the District Police Office, Solukhumbu. Both aircraft had taken off from Lukla Airport, the gateway to Mount Everest.

Police Inspector Mausam Tamang said the man who died was Vasanth Kumar Balaramaramadu, a 47-year-old Indian national travelling aboard the Fishtail Air helicopter, according to a Nepal Police statement reported by The Hindu BusinessLine. Shailesh Krishna Patel, a 49-year-old Indian-origin resident of New Zealand who was also aboard the Fishtail aircraft, was injured and was airlifted to Mediciti Hospital in Kathmandu by a Prabhu Helicopter, Tamang said.

What Authorities Have Said

The chief district officer of Solukhumbu district, Kaman Singh Thapa Magar, told Reuters that the injured New Zealander had been rescued and that the incident took place in the Mount Everest base camp area. Fishtail Air said in a statement that its helicopter was carrying passengers who had been rescued from the Everest region when it crashed while landing, and a Fishtail official said the Indian and the New Zealander on board were tourists. A Dynasty Air official said its helicopter was carrying only cargo.

The Nepalese pilots of both aircraft — Rabindra Prajapati of Fishtail Air and Prajwal KC of Dynasty Air — were also injured and have been taken to Kathmandu for further treatment, police said. That brings the injured to three alongside the one man killed, a higher count than the earliest reports of the collision suggested. Police said Balaramaramadu's body has been taken to a hospital in Lukla and will be sent to Kathmandu for postmortem. The total number of passengers aboard the two helicopters has yet to be confirmed, and police said they were gathering further details.

The Setting: Peak Trekking Season at Altitude

Pheriche lies on the way to Everest Base Camp, 150 km northeast of Kathmandu, at high altitude in the Khumbu region. The collision happened in Ward 4 of Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality. The accident comes during the peak trekking season in Nepal, when helicopters ferry hikers and climbers through the Everest region — moving trekkers who have walked to base camp, and, as in the Fishtail flight's case, carrying passengers back down after rescues.

Helicopter and aviation accidents are frequent in Nepal, a pattern attributed in reporting to the country's extreme mountainous terrain, unpredictable high-altitude weather and aging infrastructure. Landing operations at small high-altitude helipads, where several operators work the same routes in the same morning windows, are among the most demanding flying in the region.

What Happens Next

No cause for the collision has been announced. Police are still confirming how many people were aboard the two aircraft, and the injured are receiving treatment in Kathmandu. For Indian families with relatives trekking in the Everest region this season, the confirmed facts so far are narrow: one Indian national killed, one Indian-origin New Zealand resident injured and hospitalised in Kathmandu, and both pilots injured. Further identification and investigation details are expected from Nepal Police and the district administration as they are confirmed.
image_caption: Mount Everest, seen from Gokyo Ri in Nepal's Khumbu region. Two helicopters collided near Pheriche, below Everest base camp, killing an Indian tourist and injuring three people.
